kurz: Planning shows at a glance which milestone is active right now, how far along it is, who is working on what, and what is not assigned to any milestone yet.

schritte.titel: Read “Where do we stand right now?”
schritte.text: At the very top of Planning › Timeline you see the active milestone with its progress (“Final version 2.0: 3 of 8 tasks done · target 20.11.”), the next target and, under “Being worked on”, which agent is working on which task. A click on a task opens it.

Each milestone is a bar from its start to the forecast. Colour AND pattern tell you how it stands: hollow with a dashed edge = planned, blue = in progress, yellow ribbed = tight, orange-red diagonal stripes = late, bluish green = done. The vertical line marked “Now” is now; hover over it to see date, time and what is running. Hover over a bar or a diamond to see title, status, progress, forecast and target date.

A click on a bar opens the milestone’s card. At the top: who owns it, status and target; below it a sentence like “5 of 15 tasks done · 1 running · 1 waiting for you · 8 blocked” and the timeline from start through today to the target (dashed: the forecast). Then “what is running, what is stuck” – grouped by cause, with the way to step in: “Answer question” when something waits for you, “Move run up” when tasks wait for a run in the queue, “Write to lead” for reviews or agents. Then the tasks themselves, open ones first, each with a small timeline (tick = created, solid = in progress, dashed = waiting) and “moved here from milestone …” when it came from another one. Requirements, design, acceptance and the order of the steps are under “Details” at the bottom.

Completed milestones are hidden so that the active ones come first. “Show completed” in the overview brings them back, faded and with ✓. In the timeline below they are collapsed under “Completed milestones”.
At the very bottom of the timeline, “Without milestone (n)” lists every open task that belongs to no milestone. Assign one: `amw aufgabe aendern <no> --bogen <no>`.

werte: number of the milestone from Planning, e.g. 45 for B45
fehler: The lead creates a task while there is an active or planned milestone. The message lists them and suggests one. Assign with `--bogen <no>` or deliberately skip it with `--ohne-bogen`.
All milestones are planned or finished. Start the next one in Planning with “Activate”.
danach: “What the computer did today” below the overview is collapsed. A click opens it; it shows which runs ran on this PC today and which are waiting.
fragen: Why is a task “running” although nobody started it?

When an agent starts a run for one of its tasks that has not started yet, AMW sets it to “running” – the task comes from the run (`--aufgabe`), from “A1234” in the description or from the branch (a1234, a1234-2). If the task is waiting for someone, or the agent is already working on another piece, everything stays as it is. To switch it off: Settings › Project › Automatic planning.
Who closes a milestone when everything is done?

When all tasks of a planned or active milestone are done (or dropped), its card shows “All tasks are done – close the milestone?” and the lead gets one notice; “Close” is under “More … · For the lead”. With Settings › Project › “Milestone done” set to “automatic”, AMW closes it itself. If a version is mandatory and none is recorded yet, it stays a suggestion with that reason. If a milestone ends with a judgement – its acceptance is a demo, a report, a trial or anything more than “all packages done” –, AMW never closes it itself, not even with “automatic”. Once all packages are done it is **ready for acceptance**: AMW writes the closing report, and the lead and the co-developer (or you, if you approve) get one notice. It is done only with the yes to the closing (Planning › Milestones › “Yes – confirm report” or `amw bogen freigeben N --art abschluss`). If new packages are added afterwards it is open again; once they are done, AMW reports it again with a new report.
What does “Move up” do?

The button at the top of the card moves the milestone up by one – ahead of the next open one before it. The lead gets a message and reorders the tasks. Activate, Close, Retrospective and Edit are the lead’s job; they are under “More … · For the lead”.
Why patterns and not just colours?

So the timeline stays readable with red-green colour blindness: the colours (blue, bluish green, yellow, orange-red) are chosen to be told apart with colour vision deficiency, and every state also has its own pattern – nothing depends on colour alone.
Why does the bar not get shorter although tasks get done?

Because new tasks were added since the start. In the milestone card under “Details › Added” you see “Since start (05.11.): +5 added · 3 done · 8 open”, and the same when you hover over the bar; “Where do we stand right now?” shows “+5 since start”. Counted as added is anything created after the start or pulled into the milestone.
Why do I have to give a milestone when creating a task?

So that nothing disappears: a task without a milestone does not show up in the overview. Agents other than the lead may not set a milestone. Their tasks stay under “Without milestone” until the lead assigns them.
Can I collect new tasks first and plan them later?

Yes: Settings › Project › “New tasks go” set to “into the inbox”. New tasks without a milestone then land in the inbox (the same as “in the inbox” in the control center); Planning shows them at the top under “Inbox (n)”. The lead deliberately pulls them into a milestone: `amw aufgabe aendern <no> --bogen <no>`. Naming `--bogen` when creating – for example because the task is needed for acceptance – puts it straight into the milestone.
What do “Milestones” and “Packages” show?

If the project has topics, Planning starts with two tabs. **Milestones** (rough planning): each milestone with its topics (from the packages that refer to them), what it ends with (demo or report) and one status – “waiting for you” or “approved”. Approve, Send back (with a note to the lead) and Earlier/Later work on the PC. You approve on your own; who else may approve you set per kind – `grobplan_freigabe` (milestones), `feinplan_freigabe` (plans), `abschluss_freigabe` (closings), each `mensch` (default) or `co+lead` (independent of who approves topics). If a kind is set to `co+lead`, the co-developer and the lead can also approve together – only with a yes from both (it shows “Yes still missing: …”), as for topics (B2913). Who approved is shown; one of them is enough to send back. Below, approved topics that have no milestone yet are listed. **Packages** (detailed planning): per milestone the packages with Who (agent or -p with model), After, Review and Cost (measured or – with ≈ – estimated from size and kind), the total on top; on the phone only the total, single costs on tap. Only the next milestone is planned in full, later ones show as “later” (see below: rolling detailed planning). Once all milestones and all planned plans are approved, “Start now” appears: the planned milestones go into implementation. The top line always shows where the project stands: “Rough planning · 1 of 4 milestones approved”, “Detailed planning · …” or “Implementation · …”. If a topic changes after a milestone was approved (new version or sent back), the milestone shows “Topic changed: TH… (version n) – check whether the plan still fits” with “Plan again” and “Hold packages not started”; the lead gets the affected milestones and packages as a task. Nothing is put on hold by itself, running packages finish (`amw thema anhalten TH… [--meilenstein N]`). If you change a milestone yourself (title, goal, acceptance, target date) or a package (title, task, criteria, milestone – in your own terminal), it does not apply at once: “Your changes – being checked” shows at the top while a fresh agent (read-only) checks the consequences. If the change touches neither goal nor success criteria nor cost, it applies by itself and you get the consequences as a note; otherwise you see old → new with the consequences and it applies only with “Yes – apply” (or “Discard”). If the check fails, it says “Check failed – yes applies it anyway”. With `themen_gegenlesen=aus` your changes apply at once as before.
When does AMW plan the next milestone in detail?

Only the next milestone is planned in full. AMW starts its detailed planning by itself: after the rough plan for the first one, then as soon as the running milestone is ready for acceptance or only its last package is running. Milestones that may run alongside each other according to the rough plan are planned together by one planner. It delivers packages with goal, topic, files, acceptance, dependencies and who runs them; AMW checks them and creates them, nothing starts. Under **Packages** you then see “Approve and start plan”: your yes is also the start – even while the previous milestone still waits for your acceptance. If the plan does not fit, have it planned again with a note (`amw bogen feinplanen N --hinweis …`); packages of the previous version that have not started are discarded. Questions from the planner go to the lead. If the planner is off or the planners' daily limit is reached, the lead plans the milestone. In the terminal: `amw bogen freigeben N --art plan --starten`.
What has the project cost so far, and what is still to come?

`amw messung --gesamt` (Workbench data: `/api/kosten`) shows the cost **so far** – measured from the cost counter of the agents in a window and the recorded runs of headless packages –, **still to come** (estimate for open packages: median of the same size and kind, minus what is already measured) and **total**. Open packages without enough measurements of the same size and kind count as “no estimate”. The costs in Planning, in the closing report and the “over forecast” message now count both sources as well.
What happens when a milestone is done?

Before it shows as “ready for acceptance”, the project's full test and a checker run: it compares every topic of the milestone with what was built and prepares the demo – both then appear in the closing report. If something is missing or the test is red, AMW creates rework in the same milestone and starts it right away; you get a note. At acceptance you can request rework instead of saying yes (`amw bogen nacharbeit N --hinweis "what is missing"`): the planner plans new packages for it, and they start without another yes.
The five gates

At the top of Planning (and on the Topics page) a bar shows all five gates: **Concept → Rough planning → Detailed planning → Delivery → Closing** – ✓ closed, ● where the project stands, ○ still to come; next to it, what the current gate still needs. AMW works the state out itself, nobody sets it by hand: - **Concept** closes when the last needed topic is approved. - **Rough planning** closes when every approved topic is in a milestone (through its packages) or has the note “nothing to build” – the lead writes the reason, the co-developer confirms it (`amw thema vermerk TH… --bestaetigen`) – and every planned milestone is approved. - **Detailed planning** closes with “Start now”. - **Delivery** closes when all milestones are done. On the way AMW only contacts the lead about deviations; if an open package costs more than 1.5 times its forecast (median of the same size and kind – with enough measurements also of the same model and effort), the lead gets one message – never for finished packages. - **Closing**: when a milestone is done – or ready for acceptance, if it ends with a judgement –, AMW writes the closing report against the success criteria – with packages and cost, leftovers (discarded packages, open criteria) and lessons (retrospective, forecast exceeded, red reviews) – and files it as a document on the milestone. The milestone then shows “Closing” with the report, “Yes – confirm report” and “Back” (with a note to the lead; after the rework `amw bogen bericht N`). The gate closes with the yes to all reports – from you, or with `thema_freigabe=co+lead` from co-developer and lead together. If something is sent back or something new is added afterwards, the gate is open again; AMW records when a gate closed or opened. In the terminal: `amw bogen tore`; co-developer and lead give their yes with `amw bogen freigeben N --art grob|plan|abschluss` (back: `amw bogen zurueck N --art … --notiz …`).
